In 1 minute

Post-call recap

Carolina · Sales Coordinator

Nine advisors at a technical school network run 5 to 7 video call presentations a day.

When it runs
At the end of each presentation video call, when the transcript becomes available in the advisor's folder, with sending expected within 1 hour
What it delivers in production
One email draft per presentation, in the advisor's inbox within minutes, with prices, terms and the agreed date taken from the call and checked against the current table.
Who decides
Drafts; the advisor reviews and sends
Effort
Calibrate on 25 transcripts; 3 weeks reviewing

# Discount rules and conditions (sales coordination)

## How to read the current table
- In current_table, the <amount> column is the amount of EACH installment; <installments> is the number of installments.
- The same course can have a different price by shift. Always use the row of the shift presented.
- The <conditions> column has the only valid campaign for that course. What is not in it is not a campaign.

## Advisor's approval authority (discount on the installment)
| Discount stated on the call | What to do |
|---|---|
| up to 10% | within approval authority, can go in the email |
| above 10% up to 20% | INTERNAL NOTE; sales coordination approval before sending; the email goes out with the table amount |
| above 20% | INTERNAL NOTE marked URGENT; the amounts block goes out only with the table |

A waiver that is not in the <conditions> column (enrollment, course materials, uniform, internship fee) is a waiver not provided for in a campaign: INTERNAL NOTE marked URGENT.

## Course not in the table
A course cited on the call that is not in the table gets COURSE NOT FOUND in the internal note, with no amounts. This applies only to that course: the course presented that is in the table keeps the normal amounts block.

## Minor
For a minor student, the email cites only the first name and the course. Age, documents, school grades and health go neither in the email nor in the internal note.

## Templates
Parent or student as an individual (type individual in the lead): template_individual.md. Company or closed class (type company): template_company.md.

## Rules with no leeway
- For a minor student, only the first name and the course appear, in any part of the output (subject, body and INTERNAL NOTE). This also applies to what the parent said on the call: CPF (individual tax ID), age, health and school grades do not appear, not even summarized.
- A question about the student's health and the advisor's answer do not become an item of "What I will take care of" or of the internal note.
- You may cite the name of the requested document (ID card, school transcript); the document number never.
- When more than one band applies at the same time (discount above 10% and a waiver outside the campaign, for example), all of them go in the INTERNAL NOTE, each with its own marking, and the amounts block goes out only with the table.

## Excluded excerpt
Whatever a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "excerpt excluded by rule", without repeating the content.

## Single pass
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and write the file to Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, draft, write). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The email never goes out without the advisor reading it, because a wrong price in writing to a parent becomes a commitment the school will have to honor or undo at a cost to the relationship. A promise outside the table or the approval authority becomes an internal note, and the advisor decides how to handle it; it does not go in the body. The Human AI does not cite data about an underage student beyond name and course, and does not attach documents.

Common mistakes

  • Copying the price the advisor said from memory instead of the price in the current table, which changes with each campaign.
  • Writing the agreed date without a time or channel; the customer waits for an email, the advisor calls, and nobody talks.
  • Using the same email for a student's parent and for a company buying a whole class.
  • Listing what the advisor will check without any deadline.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Recaps sent within 1 hour after the callfrom about a third to 85% or moreestimate based on the described routine
Draft prices and dates matching the call and the table90% or more, the calibration acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine
Advisor time per recapfrom 20 minutes of writing to 3 to 4 minutes of reviewestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Draft generated on 2026-09-02, 11:20 a.m., advisor D. Martins, call with a student's parent, Centro campus.
